classification.difficultyReason: Order three fractions by finding equivalent fractions with a common denominator.

content.prompt: Arrange the fractions from smallest to largest.

answer.worked:
Use common denominator 24.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{7}{8}&=\frac{21}{24}\\\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{16}{24}\\\frac{5}{6}&=\frac{20}{24}\end{align*}$$

Since $16<20<21$, the order is $\frac{2}{3}<\frac{5}{6}<\frac{7}{8}$.

Use common denominator 48.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{11}{16}&=\frac{33}{48}\\\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{32}{48}\\\frac{3}{4}&=\frac{36}{48}\end{align*}$$

Since $32<33<36$, the order is $\frac{2}{3}<\frac{11}{16}<\frac{3}{4}$.

Use common denominator 180.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{11}{12}&=\frac{165}{180}\\\frac{31}{45}&=\frac{124}{180}\\\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{120}{180}\end{align*}$$

Since $120<124<165$, the order is $\frac{2}{3}<\frac{31}{45}<\frac{11}{12}$.

Use common denominator 24.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{7}{12}&=\frac{14}{24}\\\frac{5}{8}&=\frac{15}{24}\\\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{16}{24}\end{align*}$$

Since $14<15<16$, the order is $\frac{7}{12}<\frac{5}{8}<\frac{2}{3}$.

Use common denominator 54.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{25}{54}&=\frac{25}{54}\\\frac{1}{2}&=\frac{27}{54}\\\frac{5}{9}&=\frac{30}{54}\end{align*}$$

Since $25<27<30$, the order is $\frac{25}{54}<\frac{1}{2}<\frac{5}{9}$.

Use common denominator 48.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{31}{48}&=\frac{31}{48}\\\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{32}{48}\\\frac{11}{16}&=\frac{33}{48}\end{align*}$$

Since $31<32<33$, the order is $\frac{31}{48}<\frac{2}{3}<\frac{11}{16}$.

The fraction lies between $\frac{5}{8}$ and $1\frac{4}{5}$; the other choices are smaller and farther away.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{4}{6}-\frac{5}{8}&=\frac{16-15}{24}=\frac{1}{24}\\\frac{9}{5}-\frac{4}{6}&=\frac{27-10}{15}=\frac{17}{15}\end{align*}$$
The smaller difference is $\frac{1}{24}$, so $\frac{5}{8}$ is closest.

The fraction lies between $\frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$; the other choices are larger and farther away.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{4}{12}-\frac{1}{4}&=\frac{4-3}{12}=\frac{1}{12}\\\frac{1}{2}-\frac{4}{12}&=\frac{6-4}{12}=\frac{1}{6}\end{align*}$$
Since $\frac{1}{12}<\frac{1}{6}$, $\frac{1}{4}$ is closest.

The fraction lies between $\frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$; the other choices are larger and farther away.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{4}{9}-\frac{1}{4}&=\frac{16-9}{36}=\frac{7}{36}\\\frac{1}{2}-\frac{4}{9}&=\frac{9-8}{18}=\frac{1}{18}\end{align*}$$
Since $\frac{1}{18}=\frac{2}{36}<\frac{7}{36}$, $\frac{1}{2}$ is closest.

The fraction lies between $\frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{5}{8}$; the other choices lie farther outside this interval.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{9}{17}-\frac{1}{2}&=\frac{18-17}{34}=\frac{1}{34}\\\frac{5}{8}-\frac{9}{17}&=\frac{85-72}{136}=\frac{13}{136}\end{align*}$$
Since $\frac{1}{34}=\frac{4}{136}<\frac{13}{136}$, $\frac{1}{2}$ is closest.

The fraction lies between $\frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$; the other choices are larger and farther away.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{47}{96}-\frac{1}{4}&=\frac{47-24}{96}=\frac{23}{96}\\\frac{1}{2}-\frac{47}{96}&=\frac{48-47}{96}=\frac{1}{96}\end{align*}$$
Since $\frac{1}{96}<\frac{23}{96}$, $\frac{1}{2}$ is closest.

The fraction lies between $\frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$; the other choices are larger and farther away.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{31}{120}-\frac{1}{4}&=\frac{31-30}{120}=\frac{1}{120}\\\frac{1}{2}-\frac{31}{120}&=\frac{60-31}{120}=\frac{29}{120}\end{align*}$$

$\frac{199}{100}$ is greater than all four choices, so the largest choice is closest.

$$\begin{align*}1\frac{4}{5}&=\frac{180}{100}\\\frac{199}{100}-1\frac{4}{5}&=\frac{19}{100}\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Four bells commence tolling together and ring every $1$, $1\frac{1}{4}$, $1\frac{1}{5}$ and $1\frac{1}{6}$ seconds, respectively. After what time will they first ring together again?

answer.short:
$210$ seconds.

Find the first common multiple of the four ringing periods.
answer.worked:
The periods are $1$, $\frac54$, $\frac65$ and $\frac76$ seconds. Since the first bell rings every second, a common ringing time $t$ must be a positive whole number of seconds.

The numbers of intervals elapsed for the other bells are $\frac{4t}{5}$, $\frac{5t}{6}$ and $\frac{6t}{7}$. These are whole numbers precisely when $t$ is divisible by $5$, $6$ and $7$, respectively.

$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{LCM}(5,6,7)&=2\times3\times5\times7\\\operatorname{LCM}(5,6,7)&=210\end{align*}$$

At $210$ seconds the four bells have completed $210$, $168$, $175$ and $180$ intervals. Thus they first ring together again after $210$ seconds.

entries.description:
In Chapter 1 we reviewed the whole numbers. This chapter is a review of fractions and decimals.

Fractions have been used since ancient times. For instance, dividing a harvest into equal parts and distributing different amounts to different families would often have involved fractions.

Fractions were used by the ancient Egyptians and Babylonians. Systematic use of decimal fractions did not appear until the sixteenth century. Decimals are now a central part of day-to-day calculations in almost every walk of life.

entries.description:
Multiplication and division of decimals by powers of 10
• When any number is multiplied by 10, each digit is multiplied by 10. This corresponds to moving the decimal point one place to the right and inserting a zero if necessary.
• Multiplying by 100 = 10² corresponds to moving the decimal point 2 places to the right and inserting zeros if necessary.
Multiplying by 1000 = 10³ corresponds to moving the decimal point 3 places to the right and inserting zeros if necessary.
• When any number is divided by 10, each digit is divided by 10. This corresponds to moving the decimal point one place to the left and inserting a zero if necessary.
• Dividing by 100 = 10² corresponds to moving the decimal point 2 places to the left and inserting zeros if necessary.
Dividing by 1000 = 10³ corresponds to moving the decimal point 3 places to the left and inserting zeros if necessary.

entries.description:
The rules for rounding are as follows.
Suppose that we want to round 10.125 89 correct to two decimal places.
• Identify the rounding digit in the second decimal place – in this case it is 2.
• Look at the next digit to the right of the rounding digit – in this case it is 5.
  • If this next digit is 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4, leave the rounding digit alone.
  • If this next digit is 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9, increase the rounding digit by 1.
  In this case, the next digit is 5, so the rounding digit increases from 2 to 3.
• Now discard all the digits after the rounding digit.
Hence 10.125 89 is approximately 10.13, correct to two decimal places. We write this as 10.125 89 ≈ 10.13 correct to two decimal places.
